endorsements.quote: Hence, any strategy that seeks to integrate AI into healthcare settings should be accompanied by robust health literacy programs capable of empowering citizens to discern between valid information, pseudoscience, and AI hallucinations, as well as to recognize when it is essential to resort to the professional judgment of the classic clinical intermediation model.

Parallel to these efforts, there is a pressing need for educational initiatives to boost both patient and provider AI literacy, empowering users to formulate effective queries, interpret AI outputs with skepticism, and recognize when professional consultation is warranted.
This reconfiguration of informational authority has profound implications for both patients and healthcare professionals.

unlisted_practices: Encourage users to verify AI-provided health information against trusted sources.
Develop guidelines for algorithmic fairness and reliability of health AI tools.
Conduct empirical research on how patients interpret AI-generated responses and how this affects clinical outcomes.
Develop standardized frameworks for integrating AI mediaries into professional healthcare workflows.
Promote digital literacy through public health education policies, continuous training for health professionals, and public awareness campaigns.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual framework/viewpoint paper examining how generative AI changes health information mediation ('AImediation') rather than an empirical evaluation.
